definitions.explanation: Colloquial term meaning that someone has been divorced two times. Formed from バツ (the X mark for "wrong") and {二|に} ("two"). The metaphor comes from the X marks once placed on a person's family register entry when they were removed after a divorce. Part of the series バツイチ (divorced once), バツニ (twice), バツサン (three times).

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧バツニだ。
バツニで⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{気|き}にしない→気にする：03026_kinisuru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Many people don't mind that someone has been divorced twice.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧バツニだ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{奥|おく}さん→奥さん：02853_okusan⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{幸|しあわ}せ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{暮|く}らしている→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧。
examples.english: He's been divorced twice, but he's living happily with his current wife.

examples.japanese: バツニになって⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{再|ふたた}び→再び：03600_futatabi⟧⟦{結婚|けっこん}→結婚：02514_kekkon⟧⟦しよう→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Some people still want to marry again even after two divorces.

notes:
バツニ is informal slang and would not appear in formal speech, news writing, or legal documents. It is most often heard in casual conversation, on TV variety shows, in tabloids, and in dating contexts (matchmaking, dating apps).

ETYMOLOGY:
The ⟦バツ→バツ：00012_batsu⟧ ("X") refers to the historical practice of striking out a name on the family register (⟦{戸籍|こせき}→戸籍：12695_koseki⟧) after a divorce. ⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧ simply means "two," indicating two such marks.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- バツニ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to become divorced for the second time
- バツニ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a twice-divorced person
- バツニ⟦{同士|どうし}→同士：03474_doushi⟧: a couple where both have been divorced twice

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦バツイチ→バツイチ：11119_batsuichi⟧: divorced once (the most common term in this series)
- バツサン: divorced three times (less commonly heard)
- ⟦{独身|どくしん}→独身：03486_dokushin⟧: single, unmarried
- ⟦{離婚|りこん}→離婚：02530_rikon⟧: divorce (the formal term)
- ⟦{再婚|さいこん}→再婚：22805_saikon⟧: remarriage

USAGE:
- More polite alternatives include ⟦{二度|にど}→二度：09503_nido⟧⟦{離婚|りこん}した→離婚する：21333_rikonsuru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ ("a person who has been divorced twice") or {再々婚|さいさいこん}⟦{予定|よてい}→予定：00824_yotei⟧ ("planning to marry for a third time").
- Avoid using バツニ to describe someone in their presence unless you know they are comfortable with the term — though playful, it can sound dismissive.
